minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 27, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on February 27, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 22, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Sachs declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

City Council Minutes  1  February 27, 2018
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Jeanne Gormick, Costa Mesa: as volunteer coordinator for Seacrest Hospice, she said she is always
looking for volunteers from different segments of the population, particularly veterans, retired
people, stay-at-home moms and those that want to give back to the community.

Michael Rotcher, M.V.: stated that staff and the Council did a very commendable job of defending
the letter and spirit of the law and insulating the City against the threat of a lawsuit in relation to
racially polarized voting. He said he was alarmed that some members of the audience didn't listen
to the presentations or deliberately distorted the facts to create issues where none existed.

Chad Kurthy, Rancho Santa Margarita: announced that he is a dispatcher with the Orange County
Fire Authority’s 911 service and he is concerned with the County’s attempt to significantly
decrease 911 staffing. He asked the City Council Members to look at the OCFA studies that he
provided them tonight and he asked for the City’s support.

Michelle J., San Clemente: declared that incorrect statements were made at the last meeting when
a Council Member said that no new roads have been built in South Orange County. She announced
that she attended tonight’s meeting to correct the record by outlining some of the newer roadways.

Ava O'Keefe, San Clemente: expressed frustration that the response she received for her recent
request for public records was a fully redacted document. She asked the Council to support its
neighboring cities in regards to the proposed toll road extension.

Mona Amirseyedian, M.V.: speaking as a member of the Community of Character Committee, she
announced that this month’s character word is “unity” and she shared some attributes that describe
the trait.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve
the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of February 13, 2018, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated February 2, 2018 in the Amount of $1,074,521.66

  Ratified the accompanying check register.
City Council Minutes  2  February 27, 2018
 3.  Check Register Dated February 9, 2018 in the Amount of $481,044.12

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Selection of Independent Auditor for the Fiscal Years Ending June 30, 2018 and June
  30, 2019

  Awarded a Contract to Davis Farr LLP to Serve as the City's Independent Auditors for the
  Fiscal Years Ending June 30, 2018, and June 30, 2019.

5.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Second Quarter 2017-18

  Received and filed.

6.  Cabling of Marguerite Recreation Center

  Authorized staff to enter into agreement and issue purchase order to West Coast Cable, Inc.
  for purchase of cabling materials and for installation services in amount not to exceed
  $62,736.96 including a 20% project contingency.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

7.  Consideration of Alternate Remedies to Respond to Racially Polarized Voting

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report and asked the Council to consider
  forming an ad hoc committee to help sort through the options and provide some
  conclusions.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: expressed opposition to an ad hoc committee and stated that the City
  needs more transparency not less. She said the public deserves open discussions not
  meetings behind closed doors .

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  form a Voting Rights Ad Hoc Committee.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Sachs indicated that he would make appointments to the committee at the next City
  Council Meeting.

City Council Minutes  3  February 27, 2018
 NEW BUSINESS

8.  Mobile Source Air Pollution Reduction Review Committee (MSRC) Grant
  Application

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 18-11 Authorizing the City Manager to Submit an Application for the
  Mobile Source Air Pollution Reduction Review Committee (MSRC) 2017 Local
  Government Partnership Program, and (2) receive MSRC PowerPoint Presentation; and
  (3) direct staff to investigate and include a priority listing of business that would like to
  have charging stations outside their business and use their private money to help subsidize
  the cost of these charging stations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

9.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Sachs presented the report.

10.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

11.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Update from Chief Vuong

  Lieutenant Quyen “Q” Vuong presented the report and discussed his efforts with social
  media engagement, bicycle enforcement, security for faith-based organizations and school
  safety. He said his goal is to conduct more community-oriented policing and to look at
  ways to make the community even safer.

  Lt. Q also introduced the City’s new Quality of Life Deputy, Dana Chaney, who discussed
  her goals for the position which include addressing homelessness, sober living facilities,
  day laborers, and nuisance neighbors in the City.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

12.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
City Council Minutes  4  February 27, 2018
   By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced that she had a lot of fun attending four Little League
opening days and watching Mayor Pro Tem Raths throw an amazing first pitch that looked like a
strike. She said she was excited to see all the kids out using the City’s fields and it was a joyful
time. She also outlined her attendance at the groundbreaking ceremony for Santa Margarita Water
District’s Trampas Canyon Reservoir in Rancho Mission Viejo. It will be the largest reservoir in
South County and will help communities with recycled water and diversified resources. Council
Member Bucknum reminded residents that this is the end of the American Heart Association’s
“Go Red” month which is designed to encourage people to get a heart health check-up.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that he was sorry to miss out on the Little League opening
day ceremonies but he was out of town with his family. He said that he too attended the
Trampas Canyon Reservoir groundbreaking and was fascinated to learn that it will hold 1.6 billion
gallons of water. It is one of the few facilities that will capture rain water and help infuse the
groundwater system, making it a significant asset to the community going forward. Council
Member Goodell thanked Lieutenant Vuong for his excellent report and welcomed him aboard.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley also discussed the Little League opening day events and said that although
she was only able to make it to two, the Council was well represented. She noted that between the
five City Council Members, there is usually at least one representative at all the major events in
town. She thanked those who make youth sports happen here in Mission Viejo and she also thanked
Mayor Sachs for allowing the Character Committee student to give her public comments when she
arrived a little bit late to tonight’s meeting. The Community of Character Committee is made up
of 20 high school students and 8 adults and Council Member Kelley thanked committee member
Mona for attending the meeting to share her thoughts about February’s character quality, unity.
She also drew attention to a new event, the Oso Fit Community Health Fair and 5k Fun Run, which
will be held on Saturday, March 3. The inaugural fair is not only a fundraiser and health awareness
event, but it is designed to raise money for Mission Viejo non-profits and Council member Kelley
encouraged residents to attend.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths said he was so proud to attend the Little League opening day events as a
City official and he enjoyed talking to the fans and parents. He noted that the fields looked perfect
and the City got a huge round of applause from the crowd. Mayor Pro Tem Raths discussed this
morning’s Chamber of Commerce breakfast meeting and he thanked City staff and Lieutenant Q.
Vuong for attending and talking to the business owners about sign regulations and safety measures.
He said he also attended Orange County Fire Authority’s Best and Bravest awards ceremony and
it was a privilege to be there watching the men and women heroes being honored.
City Council Minutes  5  February 27, 2018
 Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs agreed that the OCFA Best and Bravest awards ceremony was an inspiring event and
he discussed some of the rescue efforts that were recognized that day. He also said that the Mission
Viejo Elks Club did a nice job of honoring first responders recently. Mayor Sachs thanked
Lieutenant Vuong for arranging for him to attend an Orange County Intelligent Assessment Center
(OCIAC) meeting and said it was amazing to learn how churches, synagogues and mosques are
well aware of and attentive to all of their security needs. He noted that it was an eye-opening
presentation and opportunity and he learned quite a bit. He also shared that yesterday morning, he
held a press conference to announce his desire to engage all of the local Mayors, the Fire Authority,
the police department, schools and colleges to come together to understand and identify cracks
that allow things like the Parkland, Florida, shootings to happen. Supervisors Bartlett and Spitzer
supported the event as well as a number of Mayors, Undersheriff Don Barnes, and some of the
SMART team members from the Sheriff’s Department. Mayor Sachs said that the new website for
Secure O.C. Schools (www.secureocschools.com) has had has over 22,000 views and he is
overwhelmed and encouraged by the support he was given. He stated that the fight is not only
about guns, but is also about other ways to preempt these tragedies from happening. Mayor Sachs
said that it is important for the community to understand that the number one priority of its elected
leaders is to see that citizens are safe and that children are protected. He thanked Council Member
Bucknum for her comments about local officials having a regional responsibility and that they
need to work together with other cities to get things done. He said that in the end, it’s all about
residents and communities and making sure the growth is commensurate with the ability to manage
that growth, whether it be the environment, water, or traffic. Mayor Sachs said he knows he can
speak for his colleagues by saying that they represent Mission Viejo proudly, and South Orange
County even more so.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:53 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, March 13, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

_____________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 13, 2018

City Council Minutes  6  February 27, 2018
